mainTopic: ביטול ברוב of a fetus (the blood clot and the שליא), the פיקה size measures, and whether cancelled טומאה can 'wake up' in fish brine
overview: The amud opens by explaining why the blood-clot miscarriage of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב must be buried: burial makes it public that the mother is now exempt from בכורה. The גמרא then asks: if the clot is a real ולד, why does it not make things טמא? רבי יוחנן answers with ביטול ברוב: the fetus is cancelled out by the blood around it. He holds the same idea elsewhere, linking רבי אליעזר בן יעקב to רבי שמעון. רבי שמעון says a fetus inside a שליא dissolved and is cancelled, so the house is not טמא. Next, a משנה teaches that a dead fetus causes טומאה at the opening of the womb only once its head is the size of a פיקה (a skein of yarn). רבי יוחנן's tradition, as רבין explains it, uses a warp skein for a woman's fetus and a woof skein for an animal's fetus. A third measure, the large sack-makers' skein, sets the size of a clod of earth from a בית הפרס or ארץ העמים. Finally, ריש לקיש rules that brine bought from an עם הארץ becomes טהור through contact with a מקוה. רבי ירמיה limits this to dipping bread, because in a pot the cancelled water 'wakes up'. אביי challenges whether cancelled טומאה can return, and רב דימי begins a proof from a משנה about impure תרומה that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Burial publicizes the exemption from firstborn status
steps.stepSummary: The clot must be buried so that people know this animal is now exempt from בכורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is buried in order to publicize that the animal is exempt from the firstborn law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question it just asked: if the clot is not טמא, why must it be buried? Burial lets people know that this animal already gave birth, so its next calf is not a בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Burial here has nothing to do with טומאה. It is a public signal. If people did not know about this miscarriage, they might wrongly treat the next calf as a בכור and give it to a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: to publicize it, to make it known
she is exempt
firstborn status

phrases.english: In order to publicize it
that it is exempt from the firstborn law.
phrases.notes: Her next offspring will not count as a בכור, because this clot already 'opened the womb'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question earlier: why bury something that is not טמא?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Burial is a public notice that the mother is exempt from בכורה.

steps.title: If it is a real offspring, why is it not impure?
steps.stepSummary: Exempting from בכורה implies the clot is a true ולד, so it should be טמא by touch and by carrying.
steps.simpleTranslation: This means the clot is a full-fledged offspring. Then why does it not make things impure, neither by touching nor by carrying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices a contradiction inside רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's ruling. It challenges how the clot can count as a real ולד for בכורה but not for טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a real ולד can exempt the next calf from בכורה. But a real dead fetus is a נבלה, and a נבלה is טמא through מגע and משא. The clot seems to be treated as a ולד for one law and not for the other.

keyTerms.meaning: is that to say? (introduces an inference)
a full-fledged, proper offspring
touching, contact
carrying

steps.confusionAlert: The question does not doubt that the clot exempts from בכורה. It accepts that ruling and asks why the טומאה law does not follow the same logic.

phrases.english: That is to say that it is a full-fledged offspring,
so why does it not impart impurity
neither through contact nor through carrying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the exemption from בכורה and finds a contradiction with the lack of טומאה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling (רבי אליעזר בן יעקב) that the clot is not טמא by מגע or משא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Exemption from בכורה proves it is a real ולד, and a real dead ולד should be טמא.

steps.title: The fetus is nullified in the majority of blood
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that the fetus is real but is outweighed by the surrounding blood, so it is בטל ברוב for טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: the Sages addressed it because of nullification in the majority.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן resolves the contradiction. The fetus truly is a ולד, but for טומאה it is cancelled out by the larger mass of blood around it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both rulings now fit. For בכורה, what matters is that a real ולד came out, so the mother is exempt. For טומאה, the small fetus is mixed into a majority of blood, so the rule of ביטול ברוב cancels its טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: nullification in a majority
they (the Sages) touched upon it, i.e., addressed it

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that one object can have different outcomes for different laws. The clot is still a ולד as a category, but its טומאה is cancelled by the majority.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Because of nullification in a majority they addressed it.
phrases.notes: The fetus is cancelled out by the majority of congealed blood, so it does not make things טמא.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מִשּׁוּם בִּיטּוּל בְּרוֹב נָגְעוּ בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the two laws: the clot is a real ולד, but its טומאה is cancelled by the majority
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A real ולד must also be טמא.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is a real ולד for בכורה, but its טומאה is בטל ברוב in the surrounding blood.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן is consistent: two תנאים share one principle
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רבי יוחנן elsewhere said רבי אליעזר בן יעקב and רבי שמעון hold the same idea. The idea is ביטול ברוב of a fetus.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן follows his own reasoning, for רבי יוחנן said: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב and רבי שמעון said the same thing. The ruling of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב is the one we just mentioned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רבי יוחנן's answer matches another statement of his. It sets up a comparison to רבי שמעון, which the next steps will explain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן had already linked these two תנאים under one principle. That makes his ביטול ברוב explanation here consistent with his own view. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's half of the comparison is the clot ruling we just learned. רבי שמעון's half still needs to be identified.

keyTerms.meaning: he follows his own line of reasoning
one and the same thing (the same principle)
that which we said

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan follows his own reasoning,
for Rabbi Yoḥanan said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov and Rabbi Shimon
said one and the same thing;

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב — הָא דַּאֲמַרַן.
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov — that which we said.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that רבי יוחנן's answer in step 3 is consistent with another statement of his.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוחנן, רבי אליעזר בן יעקב and רבי שמעון share a single principle: a fetus can be בטל ברוב.

steps.title: Which ruling of רבי שמעון is meant?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where רבי שמעון said this shared idea.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the statement of רבי שמעון?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple identifying question. It is setting up the next step, which will quote רבי שמעון's source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's half was already clear. To understand רבי יוחנן's comparison, we need to find רבי שמעון's matching ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: what is it? (which statement is meant)

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon — what is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the second half of רבי יוחנן's comparison.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source of רבי שמעון's ruling that matches רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.

steps.title: The afterbirth in the house makes the house impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: an afterbirth in a house makes the house טמא, because a ולד is assumed to be inside it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: if an afterbirth is in the house, the house is impure. This is not because the afterbirth is an offspring, but because there is no afterbirth without an offspring.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins answering by quoting the משנה where רבי שמעון's view appears. First comes the opening opinion (the תנא קמא).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The house is טמא with טומאת אהל, like a corpse under a roof. The שליא itself is not a ולד. But we assume a hidden fetus is always inside it, and that fetus makes the house טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: as we learned in a משנה
afterbirth, placental sac
ritually impure

steps.confusionAlert: The house is not טמא because of the שליא itself. It is טמא because of the ולד assumed to be inside the שליא.

phrases.english: As we learned: if the afterbirth is in the house —
the house is impure.
Not because the afterbirth is an offspring,
but because there is no afterbirth without an offspring.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the שאלה by quoting the משנה that contains רבי שמעון's view.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is the משנה about a שליא in the house (נדה 18a).

steps.title: רבי שמעון: the fetus dissolved before emerging
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון holds that the fetus dissolved inside the שליא, so it is בטל and the house is טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: the offspring disintegrated before it came out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי שמעון's disagreement with the opening opinion. This is the ruling רבי יוחנן compared to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון agrees a fetus may have been there, but says it dissolved. The dissolved fetus is outweighed by the rest of the שליא, so it is בטל ברוב and the house stays טהור. This matches the clot case: a real fetus whose טומאה is cancelled by the majority around it.

keyTerms.meaning: dissolved, disintegrated
before it came out

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's principle is that a real fetus mixed into a larger mass can lose its טומאה through ביטול ברוב. He finds this in רבי אליעזר בן יעקב (the blood clot) and in רבי שמעון (the dissolved fetus in the שליא).

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
The offspring disintegrated before it emerged.
phrases.notes: So the dissolved fetus is nullified in the majority, and the house is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: וָלָד נִימּוֹק עַד שֶׁלֹּא יָצָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quoted משנה with רבי שמעון's dissent, the ruling רבי יוחנן was referring to.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fetus dissolved and is בטל in the שליא, so the house is not טמא.

steps.title: A משנה: dead fetuses need a rounded head before they make the womb a source of impurity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: a נפל does not cause פתיחת הקבר טומאה until its head is rounded like a פיקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: Dead fetuses do not have the 'opening of the grave' (the womb), until they make the head round like a skein.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a משנה about when a dead fetus starts to make things טמא. This sets up the questions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, once the womb opens around a dead fetus, it counts like a grave opening and spreads טומאה. This משנה limits that rule: a very undeveloped fetus does not count until its head reaches a certain round size. The rest of the sugya is about what that size is.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned elsewhere (in a משנה from another place)
Fetuses that were born dead or are not viable
The opening of the 'grave', meaning the opening of the womb
Like a פיקה: a rounded ball or skein of yarn

steps.confusionAlert: Here קבר does not mean a real grave in the ground. It refers to the mother's womb, which acts like a 'grave' around a dead fetus.

phrases.english: We learned there (in a Mishnah elsewhere):
Dead fetuses do not have [impurity at] the opening of the womb,
until they round out the head like a skein.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of fetal טומאה, now from a new source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נפל causes פתיחת הקבר טומאה only once its head is rounded to the size of a פיקה.

steps.title: What is meant by 'like a skein'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the measure כפיקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'like a skein'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple clarifying question about the word in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word פיקה can refer to different round objects. To know the size, we first need to know which object is meant.

keyTerms.meaning: What is? (a request for a definition)

phrases.english: What is 'like a skein'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a definition of the term in Step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which object, and what size, the word פיקה refers to.

steps.title: רב הונא: a skein of wool
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that it is a skein of wool.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: Like a skein of wool.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives a first answer: the פיקה is a ball of wool yarn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This narrows down the material but not the exact size. That gap leads directly to the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: Wool

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
Like a skein of wool.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פיקה is a skein of wool.

steps.title: חייא בר רב asks: a skein of warp or of woof?
steps.stepSummary: חייא בר רב asks רב הונא whether he means a skein of warp threads or of woof threads.
steps.simpleTranslation: חייא בר רב said to רב הונא: My teacher, explain: of warp or of woof?
steps.whatsHappening: A student asks רב הונא to be more exact about which kind of wool skein he means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Weavers kept two kinds of thread wound into skeins: שתי (the lengthwise warp) and ערב (the crosswise woof, which is thicker). The two skeins differ in size, so 'wool' alone does not fix the measure.

keyTerms.meaning: Warp: the lengthwise threads on a loom
Woof (weft): the crosswise threads, which are thicker
Explain! Make it clear

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ חִיָּיא בַּר רַב לְרַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Chiyya bar Rav said to Rav Huna:
My teacher, explain:
of warp or of woof?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ חִיָּיא בַּר רַב לְרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for more detail on רב הונא's answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the wool skein is a warp skein or a woof skein.

steps.title: A ברייתא: רבי מאיר says warp, רבי יהודה says woof, רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק says when טפיפיות appear
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers with a ברייתא that records a three-way מחלוקת.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It was taught: A skein of warp, the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: of woof. רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק says: from when טפיפיות are seen.
steps.whatsHappening: Instead of choosing one himself, רב הונא quotes a ברייתא where תנאים already argue about this exact point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר says a warp skein and רבי יהודה says a woof skein. רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק uses a different kind of marker altogether: a visible sign (טפיפיות) instead of a yarn-size comparison.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
A visible sign at the womb-opening (defined in Step 14)

phrases.english: He said to him: It was taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: פִּיקָּה שֶׁל שְׁתִי, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.english: A skein of warp; these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yehuda says: of woof.
Rabbi Eliezer son of Rabbi Tzadok says:
From when tefifiyot are seen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers חייא בר רב by citing a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is a מחלוקת: רבי מאיר says warp, רבי יהודה says woof, and רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק says from when טפיפיות appear.

steps.title: What are טפיפיות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the unusual word טפיפיות.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are טפיפיות?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to define the rare word used by רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His opinion cannot be understood until we know what sign he is describing.

phrases.english: What are tefifiyot?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a definition of a term from Step 12.

steps.title: How they explained טפיפיות in Jerusalem: like a mule bending down
steps.stepSummary: Through שמואל, רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק's own explanation is reported: it looks like a mule crouching to urinate, with one round shape appearing inside another.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל, in the name of רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק: This is how they would explain it in Jerusalem: Like a mule that crouches to pass water, and a skein appears from within a skein.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a picture to explain טפיפיות: the folds of skin look like a round ring coming out from inside another ring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The explanation comes from the same תנא who used the word, passed down through שמואל. It shows that his sign is still a round, skein-like look, but it is judged by appearance instead of by matching a yarn size.

keyTerms.meaning: A female mule
Crouching, bending down
A round 'skein' appearing from within another one

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said
in the name of Rabbi Eliezer son of Rabbi Tzadok:
This is how they would explain it in Jerusalem:
Like a mule that crouches to pass its water,
and a skein appears from within a skein.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: טפיפיות are folds that look like a mule crouching to urinate, so that one round shape appears inside another.

steps.title: רב הונא heard of two skeins but cannot say what each is for
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא reports a tradition of two פיקה measures, warp and woof, but does not know where each one applies.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: I heard of two skeins, one of warp and one of woof, and I am not able to explain them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא admits that he received two measures without knowing what each is used for. This sets up the explanations that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now, warp and woof looked like an argument between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה. רב הונא's tradition suggests that both measures may be correct, each for a different case, but he does not know which case is which.

keyTerms.meaning: I heard (I received a tradition)
And I cannot explain it

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: שָׁמַעְתִּי שְׁתֵּי פִּיקוֹת,
phrases.english: Rav Huna said: I heard of two skeins,

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת שֶׁל שְׁתִי וְאַחַת שֶׁל עֵרֶב,
phrases.english: one of warp and one of woof,
and I am not able to explain them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: שָׁמַעְתִּי שְׁתֵּי פִּיקוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a tradition that may change how the warp/woof views are understood.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a tradition of two separate פיקה measures, warp and woof, whose uses are unknown.

steps.title: רב דימי reports that רבי יוחנן heard of three skeins
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי brings from ארץ ישראל that רבי יוחנן knew of three פיקה measures, including a large sack-makers' skein, but also could not explain them.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said that רבי יוחנן said: I heard of three skeins: one of warp, one of woof, and one of a large skein of sack-makers, and I am not able to explain them.
steps.whatsHappening: A report from ארץ ישראל adds a third measure, but no one has yet said what each measure is for. Steps 17 and 18 explain them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there are three measures with no explanation. This builds tension that רבין resolves in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: When רב דימי came (from ארץ ישראל to Bavel)
Sack makers

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
I heard of three skeins,

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת שֶׁל שְׁתִי וְאַחַת שֶׁל עֵרֶב
phrases.english: one of warp and one of woof

phrases.aramaic: וְאַחַת שֶׁל פִּיקָּה גְּדוֹלָה שֶׁל סַקָּאִין,
phrases.english: and one of the large skein of sack makers,
and I am not able to explain them.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands רב הונא's two measures to three.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן received three פיקה measures (warp, woof, and the large sack-makers' skein) without knowing their uses.

steps.title: רבין explains: warp for a woman, woof for an animal
steps.stepSummary: רבין reports רבי יוחנן's explanation: a human fetus needs the warp measure and an animal fetus needs the woof measure.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came, he explained it in the name of רבי יוחנן: For a woman, like the one of warp; for an animal, like the one of woof.
steps.whatsHappening: The puzzle of רבי יוחנן's tradition is solved: the warp measure and the woof measure each apply to a different kind of fetus.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The warp skein is the measure for a human fetus, and the woof skein is the measure for an animal fetus. This shows the two measures can work side by side, and it ties the topic to animals, which is the subject of מסכת בכורות.

keyTerms.meaning: When רבין came (from ארץ ישראל)
He explained it
An animal

steps.whatToRemember: Head the size of a warp skein is the measure for a woman's fetus. Head the size of a woof skein is the measure for an animal's fetus.

phrases.english: When Ravin came,
he explained it in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
That of a woman is like that of warp,
that of an animal is like that of woof.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין פֵּירְשַׁהּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the explanation that רב הונא and רב דימי's report were missing.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The warp measure is for a human fetus and the woof measure is for an animal fetus.

steps.title: The large sack-makers' skein: the measure for a clod of impure earth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא identifies the third measure from a תוספתא: a clod of earth from a בית הפרס or ארץ העמים is טמא when it is the size of the large sack-makers' skein.
steps.simpleTranslation: The large skein of sack makers: as we learned: A clod of earth that comes from a בית הפרס or from ארץ העמים, its measure is like a large skein of sack makers, which is like the seal of large sacks, and that size is found on the top side of the stopper of a Bethlehem jug.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the puzzle by showing where the third measure, the large sack-makers' skein, is used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This third measure has nothing to do with fetuses. It sets how big a clod of earth from a place of doubtful טומאה (a בית הפרס, or land outside ארץ ישראל) must be in order to be טמא. The גמרא adds two familiar objects, a sack seal and a jug stopper, to show the size.

keyTerms.meaning: A clod of earth
An area where a grave was plowed over, so bones may be scattered there
Lands outside ארץ ישראל, which חז"ל declared טמא
Large sacks
The stopper or seal of a jug

steps.whatToRemember: There are three פיקה measures: warp for a woman's fetus, woof for an animal's fetus, and the large sack-makers' skein for a clod of earth from a בית הפרס or ארץ העמים.

phrases.english: The large skein of sack makers is as we learned:

phrases.aramaic: גּוּשׁ הַבָּא מִבֵּית הַפְּרָס, מֵאֶרֶץ הָעַמִּים —
phrases.english: A clod of earth that comes from a beit haperas, or from the land of the nations,
its measure is like a large skein of sack makers,
which is like the seal of large sacks,
and it is found on the upper side
of the stopper of a Bethlehem jug.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבין's explanation by identifying where the third measure applies.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The large sack-makers' skein is the size needed for a clod of earth from a בית הפרס or ארץ העמים to be טמא.

steps.title: Brine from an unreliable seller becomes pure through contact with water
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש, in the name of רבי יהודה נשיאה, rules that one who buys ציר from an עם הארץ can make it טהור by touching it to מקוה water.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said in the name of רבי יהודה נשיאה: Someone who buys fish brine from an עם הארץ lets it touch water, and it is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a ruling: brine bought from someone who is careless about טומאה can be purified just by letting it touch a מקוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עם הארץ is not trusted about טהרה, so his brine might be טמא. The ruling says you do not need to throw it out. Bringing it into contact with מקוה water (השקה) is enough. Why this works is explained in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Major אמורא of ארץ ישראל, the study partner of רבי יוחנן
A grandson of רבי יהודה הנשיא who served as נשיא
Fish brine, the liquid that comes out of salted fish
Someone not trusted to be careful about טומאה and טהרה
He brings it into contact (השקה) with the water of a מקוה

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה נְשִׂיאָה:
phrases.english: Reish Lakish said in the name of Rabbi Yehuda Nesia:
One who buys fish brine from an am ha'aretz,
phrases.notes: The seller is not trusted about purity, so the brine may be impure.

phrases.english: lets it touch water, and it is pure.
phrases.notes: The water meant here is that of a מקוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה נְשִׂיאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic, unrelated to the פיקה measures discussed just before.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Brine bought from an עם הארץ becomes טהור through השקה with מקוה water.

steps.title: Why it works either way: majority water or majority brine
steps.stepSummary: The ruling is explained with a ממה נפשך argument. If most of the liquid is water, השקה purifies it. If most is brine, brine cannot become טמא at all, and the small amount of water is בטל in the majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whichever way you look at it: if most of it is water, then once he made it touch the מקוה, the water became pure. And if most of it is brine, brine cannot become impure at all. So what impurity is left? Only the small amount of water, and that small amount is cancelled out by the majority.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind the ruling. Either possibility about what is in the brine leads to the same result: it is טהור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Brine sold in the market is a mix of real fish liquid and water. Case 1: mostly water. Water can be purified by touching a מקוה, so the whole mix becomes pure. Case 2: mostly brine. Pure fish brine cannot receive טומאה, and the little water in it is בטל ברוב, so it does not count. Either way, nothing impure remains.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Whichever way you take it.' An argument that every option leads to the same result
Touching a liquid to מקוה water, which purifies water
Cannot receive טומאה at all
Cancelled out by the majority (ביטול ברוב)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think השקה purifies the fish brine itself. Brine never needed purifying, because it cannot become טמא. Only the water part needed help, either through השקה or by being בטל in the majority.

phrases.english: Whichever way you look at it:
if water is the majority,

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּעָבֵיד לְהוּ הַשָּׁקָה טָהֲרִי לְהוּ,
phrases.english: once he made them touch the mikveh, they became pure;
phrases.notes: Water is purified by contact with a מקוה.

phrases.english: and if the majority is brine,

phrases.aramaic: צִיר לָא בַּר קַבּוֹלֵי טוּמְאָה הוּא.
phrases.english: brine is not able to receive impurity.
phrases.notes: Fish brine is not one of the liquids that can become impure.

phrases.english: What impurity is there?
Only because of that minority of water,
and that water is cancelled out by the majority.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind the ruling in step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The brine is טהור in every case: majority water is purified by השקה, and majority brine cannot become טמא while the water minority is בטל.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה limits the ruling to dipping bread, not cooking
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה says the leniency applies only to dipping bread in the brine. If the brine is put into a pot with water, the nullified water meets its own kind and 'wakes up' as טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: They taught this only for dipping one's bread in it. But for a cooking pot, it does not work, because the kind found its own kind and woke up.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה adds a limit to the ruling: it works only when the brine is used as a dip, not when it is cooked with water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the majority-brine case, the water was pure only because it was outnumbered and בטל. In a pot, the small impure water joins the larger amount of water in the pot. Water now outnumbers the brine, so the cancelled water comes back to life as טמא. This idea is called מצא מין את מינו וניעור.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא of ארץ ישראל
'They taught this only…' A formula that limits a ruling
A cooking pot
A substance meets its own kind and 'wakes up.' Something בטל becomes significant again

steps.whyThisMatters: This step sets up the main question of the rest of the sugya: can something that was בטל come back to life?

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא לִטְבּוֹל בָּהֶן פִּיתּוֹ,
phrases.english: They taught this only for dipping his bread in it,
but for a cooking pot, no,
phrases.notes: Here the brine is cooked together with other water.

phrases.english: because the type found its own type and was revived.
phrases.notes: The impure water joins the pot's water and is no longer a minority.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא לִטְבּוֹל בָּהֶן פִּיתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits how far the ruling of steps 19-20 reaches.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The purification works only for dipping bread. In a pot with water, the nullified water wakes up as טמא.

steps.title: אביי asks: can nullified impurity really come back?
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי teaches רבי ירמיה's ruling, and אביי challenges it: once טומאה has been בטל, how can it return?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב דימי was sitting and saying this teaching. אביי said to him: Does impurity that was cancelled really come back and wake up?
steps.whatsHappening: While רב דימי repeats רבי ירמיה's teaching, אביי objects to its basic idea, that cancelled טומאה can return.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's view is that ביטול should be final. Once the water was cancelled in the majority brine, it counts as pure. Adding more water later should not undo that. The challenge targets the principle of ניעור, not the facts of the case.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who often brought teachings from ארץ ישראל to בבל
A leading אמורא of בבל
A teaching or halachic tradition
'Does it really come back and wake up?' A challenging question

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רַב דִּימִי וְקָאָמַר לְהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא.
phrases.english: Rav Dimi was sitting and saying this teaching.
Abaye said to him:
Does impurity that was nullified come back and revive?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the principle behind רבי ירמיה's limitation in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ירמיה's claim that the cancelled water wakes up in a pot (מצא מין את מינו וניעור).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ביטול should be permanent. Once the טומאה was cancelled, adding more of the same kind should not bring it back.

steps.title: רב דימי begins a proof from a משנה about impure תרומה
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי answers אביי: don't you agree with this idea yourself? He begins to cite a משנה about a סאה of impure תרומה that fell into a mixture. The quote continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: And you, don't you agree with this? But we learned in a משנה: A סאה of impure תרומה that fell…
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי pushes back and begins bringing a משנה to prove that cancelled things can wake up. This step only opens the proof, and the rest of the quote comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of arguing from logic, רב דימי answers אביי's challenge by pointing to a משנה that he believes אביי already accepts. The case is a סאה of impure תרומה falling into a larger amount. The details that prove ניעור appear on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Don't you also hold this?' Pointing out that the challenger already accepts the idea
'But we learned in a משנה…' Introduces a proof from a משנה
A unit of volume measure
תרומה that became טמא, which may not be eaten by a כהן

steps.confusionAlert: The proof is cut off in the middle of the sentence. Do not try to work out its conclusion yet. The rest of the משנה comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: He said to him: And you, do you not hold this?
But didn't we learn in a mishnah:
A se'a of impure teruma that fell…
phrases.notes: משנה תרומות ה:ב. The quote continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to אביי's challenge in step 22 with a source-based proof.
steps.raayaObject: That cancelled טומאה can wake up again (ניעור).
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה תרומות ה:ב, about a סאה of impure תרומה that fell into a mixture. The quote continues on the next amud.
